name: iecode
description: Structured Text for TwinCAT in VS Code: edit .TcPOU/.TcDUT/.TcGVL/.TcIO as plain ST, browse and extend PLC projects, workspaces with libraries and applications, view and edit .TcVIS visualizations, text lists (.TcGTLO), image pools (.TcIPO) and the visualization manager (.TcVMO), build and deploy with the iecode CLI.
author: Jan Junklewitz

untrustedWorkspaces.description: IECode runs the iecode CLI and git on the workspace's projects.

customEditors.displayName: IECode Text List / Image Pool / Task / Visualization Manager Editor

iecode.configDiff.hidden.markdownDescription: Categories and noise kinds hidden in **Config Changes** (the checkboxes in the panel write this setting).

iecode.openAsST.description: Open TwinCAT object files as Structured Text instead of XML.

enumDescriptions: Members in the TwinCAT folders of the POU (as in TwinCAT XAE)
Methods, Properties, Actions and Transitions as groups
iecode.memberGrouping.description: How methods, properties and actions are shown below a function block, program or interface in the IECode project tree.

iecode.projects.autoReveal.description: Select the object of the active editor in the IECode project tree (also for PLC projects and library objects).

iecode.greenComments.description: Show comments in Structured Text green, also in themes that render comments grey. Not applied in high contrast themes; turn off to use the theme's (or your own token) colors.

iecode.cliPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `iecode` CLI. Empty: `iecode` from PATH.

iecode.syncProjectFiles.markdownDescription: Keep the `.plcproj` in step with TwinCAT object files (`.TcPOU`, `.TcDUT`, `.TcGVL`, `.TcIO`, `.TcTTO`, `.TcVIS`, `.TcGTLO`, `.TcTLO`, `.TcIPO`, `.TcGIPO`, `.TcVMO`) and folders created, deleted, renamed or moved in VS Code (explorer, paste, drag and drop). An empty new `.TcPOU`/`.TcDUT`/`.TcGVL`/`.TcIO` gets a template named after the file; a copied object takes the file's name and new ids. Changes made by other programs (git, TwinCAT) are not touched.

iecode.stage.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show **Stage Method** above every changed method, property or action in the Structured Text view. It stages only that section of the object file; the index is written with git plumbing, so the rest of the file stays unstaged. Nothing is shown for a view or XML editor with unsaved edits, an untracked file or a file with merge conflicts.

iecode.analysis.markUnused.markdownDescription: Mark objects and members that no PLC task can reach: **unused** in the project tree and a faded hint in the Structured Text view. Findings are hints, never errors, and say how sure they are. Library projects, interface implementations and overrides are never marked. The analysis starts when a PLC project is expanded; turn this off to skip it.

iecode.analysis.rootObjects.markdownDescription: Objects or members that count as entry points for the object analysis in addition to the PLC tasks (names or globs with `*` and `?`, case-insensitive, e.g. `FB_Plugin_*` or `FB_Motor.Start`). Use it for code that is only reached from outside the PLC project.

iecode.analysis.rootPragmas.markdownDescription: Pragma attributes (`{attribute 'name'}`) that make an object or member an entry point for the object analysis, because the runtime or a client calls it without any code reference.

iecode.blame.enabled.markdownDescription: Show who last changed each method, property, action or accessor above it in the Structured Text view, and the author of a line on hover. Counted on the lines of the view, not on the XML. Off by default because every opened view costs a `git blame` of the object file. A view with unsaved edits shows nothing until it is saved.

iecode.lint.enabled.markdownDescription: Check PLC object files on open and save and show the findings in the Problems panel: structure of the XML (bad or duplicate GUIDs, a method name that differs from its declaration, orphaned LineIds, merge conflict markers) and object-oriented rules (override and interface signatures, FINAL, ABSTRACT instantiation). Run **IECode: Lint Objects** to check the whole workspace.

iecode.lint.rules.markdownDescription: Severity per lint rule id (`error`, `warning`, `info`, `hint`) or `off`. Rules: `xml-parse`, `merge-conflict`, `guid-format`, `guid-unique`, `name-mismatch`, `file-name-mismatch`, `member-structure`, `lineids-orphan`, `naming-prefix`, `signature-mismatch`, `final-violation`, `abstract-instantiation`, `unresolved-base`, `io-dead-link`, `io-type-changed`, `io-unlinked`, `io-channel-twice`, `io-channel-twice-weak`, `io-not-built`, `io-links-incomplete`.

iecode.lint.namingPrefixes.markdownDescription: Name prefix per object kind, for the hint rule `naming-prefix`, e.g. `{ "FUNCTION_BLOCK": "FB_", "INTERFACE": "I_", "STRUCT": "ST_", "ENUM": "E_" }`. Kinds: FUNCTION_BLOCK, PROGRAM, FUNCTION, INTERFACE, STRUCT, UNION, ENUM, ALIAS, GVL. Nothing is checked while this is empty.

iecode.checkProjectFiles.markdownDescription: Check every `.plcproj` against the files on disk and show what doesn't match in the editor and the Problems panel: entries of files and folders that don't exist, duplicate entries, paths whose case differs from the disk, and object files no `<Compile>` entry lists. Quick fixes repair single entries; **IECode: Resolve Project File** repairs the whole file.

iecode.tcVersion.markdownDescription: TwinCAT version for build and activate: `auto`, `4024`, `4026` or an exact build like `4024.66`.

iecode.platforms.markdownDescription: Target platforms to build, e.g. `TwinCAT RT (x64)`. Empty: the active platform.

iecode.restartAfterActivate.description: Restart TwinCAT in run mode after activating.

iecode.libraryOutput.description: Folder (relative to the solution) for saved libraries.

iecode.showXae.description: Show the TwinCAT XAE window while the CLI works (debugging).

iecode.libraryRepository.markdownDescription: TwinCAT library repository folder (`<vendor>/<library>/<version>`). Empty: `%TWINCAT3DIR%\Components\Plc\Managed Libraries`.

iecode.librarySources.markdownDescription: Extra folders with library files named `<Name>_<Version>.library` (e.g. a shared drive).

enumDescriptions: Claude Code when installed, else GitHub Copilot Chat, else the clipboard.
Open GitHub Copilot Chat with the context prefilled (you send it).
Copy the context and open Claude Code; paste it there.
Only copy the context to the clipboard.
iecode.aiChat.markdownDescription: Where **Add to AI Chat** and **Comment for AI…** send code and visualization elements.

enumDescriptions: Open the IECode output when a CLI command (build, check, activate …) starts.
Open it only when a command fails or reports warnings.
Don't open it by itself (View › Output › IECode).
iecode.revealOutput.markdownDescription: When the **IECode** output channel opens by itself. It lists every CLI run with its progress, the compiler errors, warnings and messages, and the result; filter by level in the Output view.

iecode.ads.target.markdownDescription: Target of the **ADS Watch** view: `local` or an AMS NetId (six numbers, e.g. `192.168.1.10.1.1`). Changing it reconnects.

iecode.ads.port.markdownDescription: ADS port of the PLC runtime for the **ADS Watch** view (`851` = first PLC of TwinCAT 3). Changing it reconnects.

iecode.ads.sampleIntervalMs.markdownDescription: How often watched ADS values are read, in milliseconds. Windows timers tick about every 15.6 ms, so below ~16 ms the real rate is lower; every sample carries its actual read time.

iecode.ads.bufferSeconds.markdownDescription: Seconds of watched ADS values kept for the scope and AI tools. Long windows with many variables keep fewer seconds (at most 2 million values).

enumDescriptions: AI tools cannot write PLC variables.

You confirm each AI write. Claude Code writes always show IECode's own dialog. In Copilot Chat this relies on you not choosing "Always Allow" for the ADS Write tool: VS Code then skips the confirmation, and extensions cannot prevent that.

Auto-approve: IECode writes without asking (each write is logged in the IECode output). VS Code may still ask by its own tool approval rules. While the workspace or workspace folder settings set iecode.ads.target or iecode.ads.port to something else than your user settings, each write is confirmed instead, so a cloned repository cannot choose where auto-approved writes go. The ADS Watch view shows "AI writes: auto (N min left)" while armed, or "auto expired" / "auto not armed" when each write is confirmed. Lasts iecode.ads.aiWritesAutoMinutes (default 60) from arming, then each write is confirmed again.
iecode.ads.aiWrites.markdownDescription: Whether AI tools (GitHub Copilot Chat in agent mode, Claude Code) may write PLC variables over ADS. User settings only, so a workspace cannot turn it on. Set it with **IECode: Set AI Write Access…** in the ADS Watch view.

iecode.ads.aiWritesAutoMinutes.markdownDescription: How long **Auto-approve** of `iecode.ads.aiWrites` lasts after you arm it with **IECode: Set AI Write Access…**. Afterwards every AI write is confirmed again until you arm it again. Changing it changes the current arming too: a lower value can end it at once, a higher one extends it.

iecode.ads.aiWritesArmedAt.markdownDescription: Set by **IECode: Set AI Write Access…**: when you last chose Auto-approve (cleared when you choose Off or Confirm). It is cleared only by choosing Off or Confirm in **IECode: Set AI Write Access…**, so editing `aiWrites` by hand does not clear it. Not meant to be edited; a time in the future is ignored. Not synced with Settings Sync, so each PC is armed on its own.

iecode.ads.presets.markdownDescription: Named member lists for the AI tool **ADS Preset**: name -> member names read below a path in one call, e.g. {"sequencer": ["nStep", "sStepText", "sError", "bBusy"]}. Nothing is built in; the members follow your own naming.

iecode.ads.aiWritePaths.markdownDescription: Path prefixes AI tools may write, e.g. `MAIN.Sim` or `GVL.Test`. A prefix matches the symbol itself and everything below it, not other names that merely start with the same letters. Empty (default): every symbol is allowed. User settings only, so a workspace cannot widen it. The list limits symbol names, not machines: it does not say which PLC a name is written on.

iecode.ads.persistentPaths.markdownDescription: Extra path prefixes of persistent or configuration data, e.g. `GVL.Persistent`. Variables the build output (`.tmc`) marks as PERSISTENT are guarded without being listed; this list adds names the build output does not mark. AI writes to guarded data are refused unless the call sets `confirmPersistent: true`, and the confirmation marks them. Same matching as `iecode.ads.aiWritePaths`. User settings only.

iecode.ads.logDirectory.markdownDescription: Folder with the TwinCAT log files, read by the AI tool **ADS Log**. User settings only; a workspace value is ignored. The log of the machine this editor runs on, not necessarily of the ADS target. Must be a full path.

id.description: Unique id; a user format with the id of a built-in format replaces it.

entry.markdownDescription: Regular expression for the first line of an entry, with the optional named groups `seq`, `time`, `level`, `source` and `message` (lines that don't match continue the previous entry).

timeFormat.markdownDescription: Format of the `time` group with the tokens `yyyy`, `MM`, `dd`, `HH`, `mm`, `ss` and `SSS`, e.g. `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS`.

levels.markdownDescription: Maps the text of the `level` group to a level.

ignore.description: Regular expression for lines to skip.

iecode.logViewer.formats.markdownDescription: Log formats of the **Log Viewer**, tried before the built-in ones. Only the first 8 KB of a line are matched. **Caution:** a regular expression with catastrophic backtracking (e.g. nested quantifiers like `(a+)+`) blocks VS Code while a file is scanned.

iecode.logViewer.gapSeconds.markdownDescription: The **Log Viewer** marks a gap above an entry that comes more than this many seconds after the previous one. `0` turns the marks off.

iecode.logViewer.groupRepeats.markdownDescription: The **Log Viewer** shows consecutive repeats of the same entry (same source, level, message and continuation lines) as one row with a count.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No TwinCAT projects found in this workspace.
Open a folder with a .sln, .tsproj or .plcproj, or add one to the workspace.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)

No variables watched. Add PLC variables to see their live values over ADS (target: iecode.ads.target).
[Add Variable…](command:iecode.adsWatchAdd)
Or right-click a variable in the ST editor › Add to ADS Watch.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_symbols
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find PLC variables (ADS names and types) in the build output of the workspace PLC projects.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists ADS symbol names and their types from the build output (.tmc) of the TwinCAT PLC projects in the workspace whose name contains the filter (case-insensitive), optionally narrowed by prefix and type, at most 100 per call (continue with offset). Use it to find the exact ADS name (e.g. MAIN.fbMotor.bEnable) before watching, reading or writing a variable. Projects that were never built are reported as not listed. Members of array elements are not listed unless the prefix names the element (MAIN.afbMotor[2].). With enumType it returns the members and values of that enum type instead (valid values for ads_write and ads_wait); with hidden: true it also lists variables marked {attribute 'hide'}, which have no ADS symbol. A project without a build output is listed from the running PLC when a filter or prefix is given, else from the source code (see source); the first lines of the answer name the source.

filter.description: Part of the ADS name to search for, e.g. "MAIN." or "nCounter"; empty lists the first 100.

enumType.description: Name of an enum type, e.g. E_Mode: returns its members with values, so valid values for the write and wait tools are known.

hidden.description: Also list variables marked {attribute 'hide'}: they have no ADS symbol and cannot be read.

prefix.description: Start of the ADS name; a trailing dot, e.g. MAIN.fbMotor., lists only the direct members of that instance with their types. The members of one array element are listed only when the prefix names it, e.g. MAIN.afbMotor[2]. (every element has the same members).

type.description: Only symbols of this type, e.g. BOOL or FB_Drive; arrays match their element type.

offset.description: Skip this many matches; pages are 100 rows.

limit.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100 (default 100). A small limit keeps a narrow look-up cheap; continue with offset.

source.description: Where the list comes from. auto (default) uses the build output of each PLC project and falls back to the running PLC (a filter or prefix is needed, at most 500 matches) and then to the source code; the result always says which source it used.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_watch
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add or remove PLC variables in the ADS Watch list (live values).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds or removes ADS symbols in the ADS Watch list, whose values are then sampled continuously (every iecode.ads.sampleIntervalMs, default 100 ms) for the read and scope tools. Returns what the call added and removed plus the count; call it with no arguments, or with list: true, for the full list with types and per-symbol errors. Entries you add are marked as added by AI; you can remove only those, unless you pass force: true with remove, which asks the user once to confirm removing their entries. clearAi: true removes all entries you added. Entries can be put in named groups (add with group); a group can be switched off (group with enable: false) so its symbols are not sampled but stay in the list, or removed (group with removeGroup: true). A symbol in two groups is sampled while one of them is on. Watch a variable before asking for its history. With expand: true, a structure in add is replaced by its members (at most 200).

add.description: ADS names to watch, e.g. MAIN.nCounter.

remove.description: ADS names to stop watching (only entries added by AI).

list.description: Return the full list with types and errors. Default: only what this call changed, plus the count.

clearAi.description: Remove every entry you added (the user's entries stay; entries a running wait uses stay until it ends). Cannot be combined with add or remove.

force.description: With remove: also remove entries the user added, after the user confirmed in a dialog. Without it only your own entries can be removed.

group.description: Name of a group. With add: the added symbols join the group (and a switched-off group is switched on). With enable or removeGroup: the group to switch or remove. Only entries you added can be in a group.

enable.description: With group: true samples the group again, false stops sampling its symbols without removing them.

removeGroup.description: With group: remove the group and the entries that belong to no other group.

expand.description: Add the members of a structure instead of failing; at most 200 members.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_read
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read current values of PLC variables over ADS.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the current values of ADS symbols on the configured target (iecode.ads.target). Watched symbols come from the live sample buffer, others are read once. Without symbols, all watched symbols are returned. A structure, function block instance or array is returned as the list of its members (see depth); the result says what was left out.

symbols.description: ADS names to read; default all watched symbols.

depth.description: How many levels of nested structures to read, default 3; a structure or array is returned as a list of its members, at most 200 members and 20 array elements.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_scope
languageModelTools.userDescription: Summarize how watched PLC variables changed over the last seconds.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns per watched ADS symbol over the last seconds (default 60): min, max, last value and sample count, how often it changed and when, plus a tab-separated table (time in seconds relative to the newest sample). Prefer changesOnly: true for step counters, enums, BOOLs and STRING values (one row per value change with the start value, never thinned; the plain table lists STRING values only in the summary). Use edges: true for BOOL pulses (rising and falling edges with times). maxRows limits the rows, decimals rounds fractions. A plain table over a long window is thinned and says how many samples it shows; it keeps every value change except in fast-changing columns, which are thinned evenly. Only watched symbols have a history: add them with the watch tool first and wait for samples.

symbols.description: Watched ADS names; default all watched symbols.

decimals.description: Round fractional numbers to this many decimals, 0-9 (integers stay as they are).

changesOnly.description: One row per value change instead of one per sample; also lists STRING values. Never thinned.

edges.description: List rising and falling edges of BOOL symbols with their times instead of the table; other types are named as ignored. Do not combine with changesOnly.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_wait
languageModelTools.userDescription: Wait until a watched PLC variable meets a condition.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Waits until an ADS symbol meets a condition, then returns the time and value; returns at once if the condition is already true at the first sample after the call. Conditions: = v, <> v, < v, <= v, > v, >= v, changes, contains "text". v is a number, TRUE/FALSE, an enum name, or a quoted string for STRING values. The symbol is added to the watch list for the duration of the wait if it is not watched. Resolution is the sample interval: a change shorter than one sample can be missed. Not met within the timeout is a normal result with the last value.

condition.description: Condition, e.g. = TRUE, > 5.5, changes or contains "text".

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_write
languageModelTools.userDescription: Write a value to a PLC variable over ADS (per iecode.ads.aiWrites; off by default). With "confirm" each write is confirmed unless you choose "Always Allow" for this tool.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Writes a value to an ADS symbol on the configured target and returns the value read back. This changes a running machine or PLC: only write when the user asked for it. Values are plain text in this format, not IEC 61131-3 literals (no T#1S, no 16#FF): BOOL as TRUE or FALSE (also 1 or 0); integers as decimal numbers (42, -7); REAL and LREAL with a dot (3.5, 1e-3); TIME, LTIME and TOD as [d.]hh:mm:ss[.fffffff] (00:00:01.5 for 1.5 s); DATE as yyyy-MM-dd; DT as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss; enums as the member name (any case, the exact spelling wins) or its number; STRING and WSTRING as is, without quotes. Writes are governed by the user setting iecode.ads.aiWrites: off (default) refuses with a note how the user can enable it, confirm asks the user for each write, auto writes without an IECode prompt only while it is armed (time-limited; after it lapses or when it is not armed each write is confirmed), and asks while the workspace settings change the ADS target or port. To set several values together, pass writes (1-20 items) instead of symbol and value: after one confirmation they are sent in one ADS request (not guaranteed to land in the same PLC cycle) and every item gets its own result. If any value is invalid nothing is sent. Every symbol must be named once. pulseMs (10-5000) pulses a BOOL command bit: it writes the value, waits, then writes the opposite value, so a start does not depend on the PLC resetting the bit; the result says how long it was held. journal: true lists this session's writes; restore: true writes their old values back after one confirmation. Writes to PERSISTENT data (marked in the build output or listed in iecode.ads.persistentPaths) are refused unless confirmPersistent: true. Every write is logged.

value.description: New value as plain text, e.g. TRUE, 42, 3.5, 00:00:01.5 (TIME) or an enum member name.

writes.description: Several writes in one call, instead of symbol and value: 1 to 20 items, each symbol at most once.

pulseMs.description: BOOL only: write the value, wait pulseMs, then write the opposite value, all after the one confirmation; the timing is kept by the extension and is not cycle-exact. At most one write per call.
BOOL only: write the value, wait pulseMs, then write the opposite value, all after the one confirmation; the timing is kept by the extension and is not cycle-exact. At most one write per call.

journal.description: true lists what was written through the ADS tools in this session (time, symbol, old and new value, pulses, unknown outcomes). Read-only, no confirmation. Use it alone.

restore.description: true writes the old values of this session's writes back after one confirmation, newest write first, at most 20 per call, and lists what cannot be restored. Use it alone.

confirmPersistent.description: Set true only when the user asked to write PERSISTENT data (marked in the build output or listed in iecode.ads.persistentPaths); without it such a write is refused.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_config
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show or change the ADS poll interval and buffer length for this session.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Shows or sets how often watched ADS values are read (pollMs, 10-5000) and how many seconds of values are kept (bufferSeconds, 10-3600). Without arguments it returns the current values and the memory the buffer needs. A change lasts until the user edits the setting or the window reloads. The buffer stores at most 2 million values in total, so many symbols at a fast poll keep fewer seconds than asked; the result says so. A change that makes the buffer much larger asks the user to confirm.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_preset
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read a named group of members of a function block in one call.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads the members listed in a user-defined preset (setting iecode.ads.presets) below a path in one call and prints one block, e.g. the step, step text, error text and busy flag of a state machine. Without arguments it lists the defined presets. Members that do not exist are named, the others are still read. Values are read once, not watched.

path.description: ADS path of the instance, e.g. MAIN.fbSeq.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_capture
languageModelTools.userDescription: Capture the values around a PLC condition.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Waits like the wait tool until a condition is met, then returns the value changes of the watched symbols from preSeconds before to postSeconds after the trigger as one table (time 0 = the trigger). Use it for a pulse or for reading a text at the moment a sequence errors. The symbols must already be watched for the before-part to have content; the buffer must hold at least preSeconds + postSeconds (see the config tool). Not met within the timeout returns the last window and says so. Resolution is the sample interval.

symbol.description: ADS name of the trigger symbol, e.g. MAIN.nStep.

condition.description: The trigger condition, as for the wait tool, e.g. "= 40" or "= TRUE".

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for the trigger, 1-120, default 30.

symbols.description: Watched names to include; default all watched.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_log
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read new lines of the TwinCAT log file since a marker.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads lines of the TwinCAT log file written after a marker. Call with mark: true before a test step to get a marker, then call with since: <marker> to read only what was logged afterwards. filter keeps lines containing any of the given texts, exclude drops lines containing any of them (for example exclude: ["DEBUG"]); both are plain text, case-insensitive. Without since it returns the last lines of the newest file. Each result ends with the marker to continue from. A new log file (for example after a PLC restart) is followed automatically. A marker means the end of the last complete line, so a line that was still being written when the marker was taken is returned by a later call. Read-only.

mark.description: Return a marker for the current end of the log instead of lines. Cannot be combined with the other fields.

since.description: A marker returned by an earlier ads_log call.

filter.description: Keep lines containing any of these texts (case-insensitive).

exclude.description: Drop lines containing any of these texts (case-insensitive).
